sentences.text: The genus name Achillesaurus refers to Achilles' heel because diagnostic features for these animals are found in that area.
This creature measured approximately 2.7 meters in length and 1.5 meters in height, with an estimated weight of 30 to 50 kg.
Only one specimen, the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — MACN-PV-RN 1116, has been found, consisting of sacral vertebrae, four tail vertebrae, and the left femur, tibia, and ilium.
Achillesaurus is classified within the family Alvarezsauridae alongside Alvarezsaurus and Patagonykus as a basal member.
Achillesaurus lived during the Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Rio Negro, Argentina.
It lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian period.
Some researchers argue that Achillesaurus might be a junior synonym of Alvarezsaurus because the two differ only trivially despite coming from the same formation.
